card.title: BLOODY ELEVENTH
card.flavorText: The Devonshire Regiment, nicknamed "The Bloody Eleventh," was a British Army regiment active from 1685 to 1958, which participated in many wars and conflicts such as the Napoleonic Wars, the Second Boer War, World War I and World War II. In May 1942, the 1st Battalion of the Devonshire Regiment was stationed in Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) after a local troop uprising. It was then sent to Burma in July 1943, where it served with the 20th Indian Infantry Division until the end of the war. In 1938, the 2nd Battalion was stationed in Malta, where it was involved in the Siege of Malta, before later serving in Sicily and Italy in 1943. In 1944, it took part in the D-Day landings in Normandy and fought through the North West Europe campaign, up to the crossing of the Rhine, finishing the war near Hamburg. The 50th (Holding) Battalion, raised in 1940 and later renumbered as the 12th Battalion, initially served in home defense but was trained for airborne operations in 1943. It landed in Normandy by glider in June 1944, participated in the Rhine crossing, and finished the war in Germany. The Devonshire Regiment also raised the 7th, 8th, and 9th Territorial Army battalions, in addition to the 4th, 5th, and 6th. The 5th Battalion was converted into an anti-tank unit before the war, and while the others were part of the 45th Infantry Division, only the 4th Battalion saw active service outside the UK. Most battalions were used for home defense, training, or supplying reinforcements. The 4th Battalion was sent to Gibraltar in 1940, returned to the UK in 1943, and served with various divisions until the end of the war.
